content-planner.title: October Content Plan: Home Fitness for Busy Parents
rows: You don't need an hour. You need 12 minutes and a kitchen chair.

Most parents I coach think fitness means a gym membership and a free evening. Neither exists right now, and that's fine. Here's the 12-minute chair circuit my clients do while the pasta boils: 10 incline push-ups, 15 chair squats, 20-second plank, repeat three times. Save this for tonight.
Save this and try it tonight
My client lost 9 pounds without ever leaving her living room.

Sarah has three kids under 7 and hadn't worked out since 2019. We started with two 15-minute sessions a week. Twelve weeks later she's stronger, sleeping better, and chasing her toddler without getting winded. No gym. No 5am alarms.
3 things every one of my successful clients had in common
It wasn't motivation. It was: 1) a fixed 15-minute slot in the calendar, 2) workouts that needed zero setup, 3) someone checking in weekly. Motivation fades. Systems don't.

Stop doing crunches. Do this instead.

Crunches load your neck and do little for the deep core muscles that protect your back. Try dead bugs: lie on your back, arms up, knees at 90°, and slowly lower opposite arm and leg. 3 sets of 8 per side. Your lower back will thank you.

The night I served cereal for dinner

Three years ago, I served my kids cereal for dinner three nights in one week. Not my proudest moment.

The problem wasn't cooking. It was deciding. So I built a simple system: one planning session, one shopping list, and meals that reuse ingredients.

That system became the 12-Week Family Meal Plan. More on that soon.

Jen
